description: We are building a space mission design game for our challenge. Our team is fully formed and complete.
summary: Odyssey: Space Explorer Hub is a browser-based educational game that lets students learn real space science by touching it. Nine connected missions let players walk as an astronaut on the Moon and Mars, orbit Earth, bend light around a black hole, watch eclipses, lie on a carpet under a real star map, design a spacecraft as a team, land a rocket, learn about the story of our galaxy through a narrator and fly a crewed ship to Mars. Every mission shows live numbers (gravity, orbit period, mass, power, fuel) that change as the player acts. Up to four players cooperate in the Spacecraft Builder, each with a different engineer role, a shared budget and a launch vote, while a rule-based AI advisor explains problems in plain language and ways to improve the spacecraft and make it eligible to launch. It turns mission engineering and space science into an accessible, cooperative, no-install experience. This matters because many learners never see how physics and engineering decisions combine in a real mission.
details:
Project Details

What it does: The player moves through a hub of nine missions, in a guided order or freely, and an Explorer rank fills as they finish them.

  • Walk on Another Planet: jump as an astronaut on the Moon, Mars and Earth and see how gravity changes movement.
  • Planet Story Tour: Watch the Sun and all eight planets revolve in 3D while a story takes you from world to world, with the facts of each one.
  • Earth From Space: change orbit height and watch period, speed and horizon distance change.
  • Black Hole Simulator: change the mass, drop probes and fire light beams.
  • Cosmic Event Simulator: scrub time through eclipses, meteor showers and planetary alignments.
  • Stargazing Night: walk to a carpet, lie down and click real stars to see their distance, temperature and brightness. The sky is calculated from real star positions for the chosen city, date and time.
  • Spacecraft Builder: choose solar panels, batteries, radiators, cameras, sensors, antennas, comm systems and fuel tanks within mass, power, heat and cost limits. Up to four players each take a role (Systems, Payload, Power & Thermal, Budget & Ops) and vote on launch.
  • Rocket Landing: land a 3D rocket on three worlds with limited fuel and a live stopping-distance guide.
  • Become a Space Pilot: fly a crewed spacecraft to Mars with a live mission-telemetry panel.

Benefits and impact: Learners see cause and effect immediately, work in teams and need nothing to install. Sound, touch controls and a guided tour make it usable in a classroom or on a phone.

Tools and technology

  • HTML, CSS and JavaScript
  • three.js for the 3D scenes
  • Canvas 2D for the black hole, cosmic events and landing views
  • The Web Audio API for sound, which is synthesized in code with no audio files
  • PeerJS (WebRTC) for online team rooms
  • A Python script that merges everything into one page
  • Vercel for hosting

Creativity

  • You lie on a carpet and click real stars.
  • Teams share one spacecraft design, with a different role for each player.
  • Moon scenes go silent while Mars and Earth have wind, which teaches that sound needs air.
  • 3D models of an astronaut, an Orion-style capsule, an SLS-style rocket and a RADARSAT-style satellite were built in code from reference pictures.

What we considered

  • Accuracy: stars use real positions, brightness and distances, but distances, times and costs elsewhere are scaled for gameplay.
  • Accessibility: it works with keyboard or touch, in a browser, with a mute button.
  • Cooperation: teamwork is built into the Builder’s design.
  • Performance: the game is kept light so it runs on ordinary phones.
  • Originality and credit: we credit the textures, libraries and reference images, and we did not use any NASA logos or mission patches.
